userStories.title: [E17] Production regular expressions linear, not timed
userStories.description: Found in ARV-156 and rated by its security review: 12 production `[GeneratedRegex]` rules backtrack under a match timeout (Site.CodePattern, TopologyCodes.Code, FlightRules.Carrier and Codeshare, OutboundRules.PathAndQuery and Scope, EmailAddresses.Rule, EmailTemplates.Placeholder, CsvImportReader.Number, the Cronz JobsDashboardGuard rules), and three interpreted calls also check the clock (Email.cs:199, JobsDashboard.cs:30 and :32). A timeout is wall-clock time, so a loaded node can raise RegexMatchTimeoutException on a short input: it fails closed (DependencyOutage treats it as no outage, the handler answers 500 without detail, a check never passes), so this is robustness rather than security, but it can give a rare 500 or a failed start under load. CWEs to review: CWE-1333, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: Every anchored production rule above runs on RegexOptions.NonBacktracking without a timeout (captures and unanchored search work on it); the linear engine is the ReDoS bound, stated in the CWE-1333 row

TopologyCodes.Code drops its lookahead for a length check (1 to 16) plus `^[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*\z` on NonBacktracking, proven equivalent by a CsCheck property comparing old and new rules on random strings of up to 20 characters over A-Z, 0-9, '-', '\n', lowercase and non-ASCII; parity with script 0008's CHECK and varchar(16) kept

The RedactionEnricher rules keep no timeout (a timeout in a Serilog enricher would throw and could let an event out unredacted); the FloorPlanFiles backreference rule stays anchored and bounded; both are named in the CWE-1333 row with their reason
A test per rule asserts its options and infinite timeout, and each rule's accepted set is unchanged (existing tests plus a table per rule)

Likely a measurement error in the test, not the product: KafkaProduce.NewGeneration takes the generation's timestamp before calling the client factory, but the test reads MadeAt after the factory has built its Moq mock, so a slower first mock shrinks the measured gap. Read MadeAt before building the mock; no bound changes. 2026-10-14 (test-only fix before the checkpoint): this case is fixed. Both window tests (WaitForTheWindow and FailSendsAtOnceUntilRecreated) now measure between the producer's own generation timestamps, read back at the start of the client factory through a test clock that remembers the last timestamp it gave on that thread; no bound and no production code changed (a 40 ms stall injected into a mock's build moved the old measure to 758 to 762 ms and left the new one at 798 to 803 ms). Also (2026-10-16): Sensing.MqttTransportTests.Broker_Should_CloseSilentAndRefusedConnections_And_CapThemPerAddress failed once under the story gate's load ("Error while authenticating" after 9 s) and passed alone 3 of 3. 2026-10-16 (ARV-191 story gate, run 1): tests/api/security-baseline.spec.ts:128 ("a 2 MB body is refused with 401 before the server reads it") failed on its try and its retry with write EPIPE, 1 in 5 alone right after, then 40 of 40. Separately, /tmp held about 84,000 test leftovers (50,708 folders in /tmp/ariva-unit-tests alone, from ArivaHosts and IntegrationClientTests): the fixtures should delete their folders. 2026-10-19 (ARV-089 story gate, full E2E): tests/functional/validation-capture.spec.ts:1715 ("on a portrait tablet, the tablet layout works on touch in English and Arabic", 800x1280) saw tally-in-count 2 where it expected 3 and passed on the retry. userStories.title: [E6] Dead letters: text PostgreSQL accepts and a per-topic relay hold
userStories.description: From the ARV-171 security review (PASS, 2026-10-13), three non-blocking findings. (1) A NUL character or a lone surrogate in a record's key, a header name or value, or the error message makes the keep fail (PostgreSQL text refuses 0x00 in message_key, and CAST AS jsonb refuses \u0000 and unpaired surrogates in the payload), so such a record still ends on ARV-166's unacknowledged path; it needs a buggy or hostile Kafka producer, which is what the unreadable path is for. (2) A dead-letter row that fails with a broker error ends the relay pass like any broker failure; a .dlq.v1 topic that hangs (its leader away while domain topics are fine) holds each attempt up to the 45 s produce bound and can delay domain events by up to 45 s repeatedly during the short backoffs. (3) The app charts set no terminationGracePeriodSeconds (Kubernetes default 30 s) and no host sets HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout (.NET default 30 s), while one in-flight message can need the rest of its retry schedule (at most 3 x 5 s), the keep (at most 10 s) and the consumer close. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: DeadLetters.Create replaces NUL and lone surrogates with U+FFFD in the key, header names and values and the error message, and flags the letter when it did (a header naming what was replaced, never the original bytes); OutboxKeyOf uses the digest when the key held such a character; the letter's topic, partition, offset and consumer stay exact so a replay can still fetch the original record

A .dlq.v1 row whose send fails with a broker error holds back only its topic for the rest of the relay pass instead of ending the pass, so domain rows keep draining; a domain row's failure still ends the pass as today

Unit tests: a letter with "\0" in a header and in the key is kept and its row key is the digest; a lone surrogate in the error message is replaced; a failing .dlq.v1 row leaves a domain row of the same pass sent. Integration test: a record whose key and headers carry a NUL is kept at a stop and its row read back

userStories.title: [E6] A host's own disposal never dead-letters a valid message, and the broker probe names no topic
userStories.description: From the ARV-165 security review (PASS, 2026-10-14), two low findings. (F2) The stop budget covers the retry schedule and the 10 s keep but not the consumer's own time per attempt: when attempts are slow at a stop (a database stall at Npgsql's 30 s command timeout), MassTransit's stop wait can end with a message still in its retries; the host disposes its container while the bus keeps stopping in the background, the later attempts fail with ObjectDisposedException, and the final attempt keeps the dead letter, so a valid event lands in the dead-letter topic (a replay is needed), or is faulted when the database is away too. Wiki 10 section 4.5a states the case and the replay meanwhile. (Probe) KafkaProduce.BrokersAnswerAsync calls GetMetadata(timeout), which asks for every topic on the cluster; on a large or shared cluster the reply is large. A metadata request that names one topic is not the answer: Confluent.Kafka 2.15.1 documents allow.auto.create.topics as true by default for producer-type clients (the admin client is one), so naming a missing topic can create it with the broker's defaults, AMAN's topics included (seen in ARV-176's first baseline). CWEs to review: CWE-400, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: A failure caused by the host's own disposal while its endpoint stops (ObjectDisposedException from the host's services, or an equivalent signal) does not dead-letter the message: the record is left unacknowledged so it is delivered again after the restart, without opening the ARV-166 skip (prove the checkpointer cannot pass it)

The readiness probe names no topic: it uses IAdminClient.DescribeClusterAsync on the producer's handle within the same 3 s bound, single-flight and reused for 1 s, and still reports Degraded within its bound when no broker answers. A metadata request naming one topic is not used (it lets a broker with auto.create.topics.enable create the topic with broker defaults). If DescribeCluster proves unsuitable, keep GetMetadata(timeout) for all topics, whose cost is bounded at one request a second per pod

Ariva's producer and admin client configurations set AllowAutoCreateTopics = false (KafkaClientConfig), with a test proving that a send or a metadata read for a missing topic does not create it, so no Ariva client can create a topic implicitly whatever the cluster's setting; the relay and Ingest treat the resulting unknown-topic failure as the row's own failure
Unit tests for both; an integration test where a slow attempt outlasts the bus's stop wait and the message comes back after the restart instead of reaching the dead-letter topic
Wiki 10 section 4.5a no longer describes the edge case as open

userStories.title: [E17] Trojan Source check: byte order marks inside files, the rarer format characters, file names, links and the hooks
userStories.description: Found in the ARV-157 security reviews (round 1 L1; round 2 L6, L8, I4 to I7; round 3 fix 2 and its Info notes; round 4 Info; round 6 Info; round 7 Info; round 8 L1 to L3): SEC-130 (scripts/security/scan.mjs) does not refuse U+FEFF after a file's first character, an invisible zero-width no-break space elsewhere in a line. Four files hold a raw byte order mark inside code on purpose, to strip one: .claude/hooks/lib.mjs (line 58), Platform/Backplane/Ariva.Infra/Timescale/SqlScript.cs (line 35) and Platform/Backplane/Ariva.UnitTests/Persistence/SqlScriptTests.cs (line 39) as literals, and the script 0020_alert_rule.sql inside its CHECK constraints (already allowlisted line by line). The hook file is harness code that agents do not change without the owner. The rarer format characters that DisplayText.IsClean refuses are not refused either: U+034F, U+17B4 and U+17B5, U+180B to U+180D, U+180F, U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, and the variation selectors U+FE00 to U+FE0F (emoji text uses U+FE0F). A file name that is not valid UTF-8 is dropped from the list without a word (gitFiles decodes git's output as UTF-8). Symbolic links are skipped by every rule (none is tracked outside a skipped node_modules folder today). Git-ignored output outside SKIP_DIRS (.claude/worktrees, TestResults, the E2E test-results-* folders) is read too, so local runs may report false positives. A .gitattributes working-tree-encoding or filter attribute could make the checked-out text differ from what git shows. Two harness hooks need the owner: .claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs keys an approved allowlist entry on rule, path, contains, routes, reason and approvedBy, not on the whole entry, so a field added later (such as line) could change unseen (ARV-157 makes every SEC-130 entry repeat its line in contains, which the guard holds, until then); and .claude/hooks/post-edit-scan.mjs exits 0 when the allowlist cannot be loaded, so one malformed entry silences the edit-time scan for every file (the full and --changed scans still fail closed). Encodings a file can declare that SEC-130 does not read yet: an .editorconfig charset, an Emacs coding line in a // or /* */ comment, SET client_encoding or psql \encoding in SQL, chcp in batch files, and the working-tree-encoding attribute in .gitattributes (applied at checkout, so the files built can differ from the blob reviewed). U+FFFE and U+FFFF are not refused. Windows PowerShell 5.1 and cmd.exe read a file without a byte order mark in the system code page, so .ps1 and .cmd files could be held to ASCII or a byte order mark. A C# code page can still be set outside project and response files, which SEC-130 reads: MSBuild takes environment variables as properties (ENV CodePage in a Dockerfile, env: in a workflow), a command line in a workflow or script can pass -p:CodePage=, and .proj, .projitems and .csproj.user files are imported too. A project can also name a compiler response file or import a project file of any extension (CompilerResponseFile, the Csc ResponseFiles parameter, an Import of build/x.xml), whose code page SEC-130 does not read. The fail-closed checks read raw text, so three encodings of the same settings pass: HTML character references in a meta tag (a numeric reference for a letter of the label or of the word charset, 	 or =), which a browser decodes before it reads the label; XML character references and MSBuild %XX escapes in project files (a PropertyName, AdditionalProperties or Properties value naming the code page with one letter encoded); and property names assembled by evaluation (a property holding part of the name, joined in AdditionalProperties or an Output PropertyName). Judged not needed before the pilot (round 8): the web app's first meta is a literal UTF-8 one, the other HTML is not deployed, and each needs a visible build file change by someone who could already run commands through Exec.

userStories.title: [E17] A push gets its answer, not a connection reset, under load
userStories.description: Found by ARV-124a's pilot load run. A device sending full 15 KB pushes at 150 a second, far past its limit of 600 a minute, had exactly 600 accepted, but a few of the rest reached the client as a connection reset (HttpRequestException, HttpRequestError Unknown in runs 2 and 4, ResponseEnded in run 6) instead of 429 with Retry-After: 1 of 300 in run 2, none in run 3, 3 of 300 in run 4, 2 of 300 in run 6, 3 of 300 in run 7, all during the D5 burst on a 4-core machine saturated by the whole stack. Run 7, with the harness's final checks, also had one reset (ResponseEnded) on a measured sensor's push within its rate, 1 of the burst's 6,000: the resets are not tied to refusals. Not reproduced on an idle machine: a bare Kestrel answering 429 to 3,600 unread 15 KB bodies at 150 a second gave no reset, whether it drained the body or not. Ingest aborts no HTTP connection itself, so the cause is in how Kestrel ends a request whose body was not read when the machine is busy (Proposed: the drain racing Ingest's minimum body rate), or in how the client reuses a connection the server is closing (Proposed: the harness sends every device's pushes through one connection pool, where a sensor keeps its own connection; to check). Ingest logs nothing about a reset: Kestrel's connection events are below its log level. Nothing past the limit was accepted, and no answer was a 5xx; a device that sees a reset instead of Retry-After may retry sooner, and a sensor whose push was reset does not know whether it was accepted (its retry is deduplicated by its package). CWEs to review: CWE-400.

userStories.title: [E4] Zone cold start: exits of people already inside pair with another sensor's entrant
userStories.description: Found by ARV-230's pilot load run and its security review. A zone that starts afresh (go-live, a rollback to a build that refuses its snapshot, a refused snapshot, a new profile version) knows nobody inside. For about one queue dwell time, the exit of a person who entered before it has a track the engine never saw enter; FifoPartner pairs it with the earliest person another sensor of the zone holds (F5: an unknown tracked exit is someone who entered before the engine started, or under another sensor's id), and that person's own exit later counts as a duplicate. So exits are undercounted and those waits come out short until the people inside at the restart have left: a replay of ARV-230's first pilot run, whose harness started with about 180 people inside each hall zone, counted 175 of 252 exits (77 duplicates). CWEs to review: CWE-501.

userStories.title: [E17] Lazy collection loads open no connection synchronously
userStories.description: Found in ARV-242's security review (round 2, L1): NHibernate loads a lazy collection (bags are mapped lazy, subselect) with its synchronous connection open when the load runs outside a transaction, after the connection was released (the default release mode gives it back after each statement). It needs a new physical connection to hang (the pool usually hands back the idle one it just took), so the likelihood is low. CWEs to review: CWE-400. ASVS 5.0: V15.2.2.

userStories.title: [E17] Security lookups: the bound covers the first query, and a stalled connection does not hold lookups after recovery
